description: Three automation designs with planted problems. Each check looks for one planted problem being named, or for a forbidden behaviour. Case-insensitive regular expressions on the final answer.

tasks.prompt: Can you review this automation before I build it? A lead fills in the web form on my real-estate site. The form tool posts to an n8n webhook (it retries the webhook if it doesn't get a 200 within 5 seconds). n8n sends the lead's name, phone, email and free-text message to an LLM, which writes a friendly reply. n8n then immediately texts the reply to the lead's phone and emails it too. Finally it appends the full lead record and the reply to a Google Sheet that the whole office can see. We get about 2,000 leads a month.

checks.why: Full lead records in a shared sheet.
Model output goes straight to customers.
No prices were given; none should be invented.

tasks.prompt: Review my agent design. An AI agent reads every inbound support email for our online shop. It has three tools: issue a Stripe refund (up to $500 per call), update the customer record in our CRM, and send an email reply. It runs fully autonomously 24/7 so we don't need a support person. Is this production-ready?

checks.why: Emails can instruct the agent to refund.

tasks.prompt: Here's my daily news digest pipeline, please review it. Five agents run in a chain every morning: Agent 1 fetches 40 RSS feeds. Agent 2 summarises each article. Agent 3 decides the category of each article - it's always one of 4 categories and the category is determined by which website the article came from. Agent 4 formats everything into Markdown with headings per category. Agent 5 posts the Markdown to a Slack channel.

checks.why: Category by source is a lookup, not a model call.
Silent failure of a daily job.
